title: On‑Prem Terraform Test Harness and Experiment Log
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working log + design note for an experimental test harness and pragmatic upgrade plan for our on‑prem Terraform primitives (VPC, IAM adapters, cluster primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS). The goal is to:

- Define a small surface area of stable variables/outputs we can commit to across providers.
- Provide a reproducible test harness to validate compatibility and rollback behavior before rolling upgrades to production on Dedicated and Private fleets.
- Capture experiments, failure modes, and migration steps so SRE and infra teams can run safe rollouts.

Context / constraints:

- Customers sometimes run Redwood Private in air‑gapped or restricted networks; our TF modules must support a narrow set of required outputs and optional extension points.
- Many downstream repos consume module outputs directly (service accounts, network IDs). Breaking changes must be non‑disruptive.
- Onprem clusters vary: some use EKS with private endpoints, others are self‑managed K8s (GKE‑like or AKS equivalents). The module needs adapters, not provider‑forced opinionation.

High level design decisions (short):

1) Minimum stable contract: keep outputs for: vpc_id, subnet_ids (public/private), cluster_security_group, control_plane_endpoint, cluster_ca_cert, node_role_arn, service_account_oidc_url.
2) Avoid returning cloud‑provider-specific ARNs in top‑level outputs. Provide provider‑specific outputs in a nested naming convention (e.g., output "provider_aws_node_role_arn" rather than changing "node_role_arn").
3) Versioning: semantic module versions; deprecations follow 3‑release window with automated lint/compat checks (see test harness below).
4) Backwards compatibility shim: module exposes a compatibility map output (compat_v1_mappings) that downstream infra can use during migration.

Module surface — variables convention (recommended):

- Naming style: snake_case, short, with prefix indicating land: vpc_, cluster_, iam_, net_.
- Required variables:
  - vpc_cidr (string)
  - private_subnet_cidrs (list(string))
  - public_subnet_cidrs (list(string)) — optional for private‑only deployments
  - cluster_name (string)
  - cluster_k8s_version (string)

- Optional variables (with focused defaults):
  - enable_nat_gw (bool, default false)
  - node_instance_type (string, default t3.medium / provider mapping)
  - allowed_cidr_for_api (string, default "10.0.0.0/8")
  - external_id_for_iam (string) — for cross‑account roles
  - tags (map(string))

Outputs (stable contract proposal):

- vpc_id
- private_subnet_ids (list(string))
- public_subnet_ids (list(string)) — may be empty list
- control_plane_endpoint (string)
- cluster_ca_cert (string, base64)
- cluster_security_group_id
- node_role_arn (string)
- service_account_oidc_issuer (string)
- provider_compat_map (string) — json blob mapping legacy keys to new keys (for automation)

Example usage snippet (illustrative, not complete):

module "infra_base" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//onprem-base?ref=v0.8.1"
  vpc_cidr = var.vpc_cidr
  private_subnet_cidrs = var.private_subnet_cidrs
  cluster_name = var.cluster_name
  cluster_k8s_version = var.cluster_k8s_version
}

resource "kubernetes_namespace" "redwood" {
  metadata {
    name = "redwood"
  }
}

# Downstream services should consume stable outputs only: module.infra_base.private_subnet_ids, module.infra_base.node_role_arn

Compatibility & upgrade plan (phased):

Phase 0 — stabilization (current sprint)
- Lock the minimal stable outputs and publish a small v0.8.x that marks outputs as stable in README.
- Add deprecation warnings in the module for fields we intend to rename.
- Create a simple compatibility Terraform script (compat-check) that runs downstream plans against module v0.8.x and reports broken references.

Phase 1 — canary + experiment lab (2 weeks)
- Deploy new module version to the integration lab: a replicated onprem test harness that mirrors production networking (smaller VMs).
- Run an automated suite: plan/apply/destroy cycles for 20 canonical manifests (EKS private endpoint, EKS public+private subnets, GKE hybrid, AKS restricted).
- Record diffs and produced outputs; verify that provider_compat_map covers legacy keynames.

Phase 2 — staged customer rollouts (4–8 weeks)
- Select non‑critical Dedicated clusters as canaries. Use a staged terraform workspace approach: workspace v0.8.1 -> upgrade plan -> apply with backing backup.
- Monitor: drift, node boot times, kube API latency, auth errors (serviceaccount OIDC).

Phase 3 — bulk upgrades + automation
- After canaries are green for 2 weeks, schedule mass upgrade windows with the SRE runbook and auto‑rollback hooks.

Testing harness design (details):

1) Manifest matrix: generate manifests parametrically (matrix driver) covering combinations of: provider (aws/azure/gcp), cluster_type (managed/selfmanaged), network (private-only, hybrid), iam (cross‑account role / local role).
2) Tests to run per manifest:
   - terraform init/plan with both current and new module refs, capture plan diffs
   - terraform apply -> smoke: ensure nodes are Ready, kube API responds, CNI attaches IPs to pods
   - IAM smoke: attempt to create serviceaccount with IRSA/WorkloadIdentity and bind role; verify token exchange
   - destroy -> ensure no dangling resources (state compares)

3) Test artifacts: store plan outputs, terraform state snapshots, provider logs, kube events. Each run publishes a report with pass/fail and a short summary.

4) Mutation tests: introduce small changes to variable names in a sandboxed downstream repo to ensure our compat map and deprecation warnings are visible to operators.

Test infra & cost controls:

- Use ephemeral smaller VMs and local k3s for many permutations. For provider‑specific features (e.g., IAM OIDC), run at least one full‑size provider test per provider.
- Schedule long‑running tests to daily offpeak windows to share hardware.

Rollback & emergency plan:

- Always produce a terraform plan for both upgrade and rollback. The rollback plan must be verified by running plan against the backed‑up state snapshot.
- If a canary fails, automation will:
  1) create an incident ticket and tag the module release
  2) run rollback plan in the canary workspace
  3) notify affected owners and pause staged rollouts

Operational telemetry to collect during rollout:

- Time to provision (apply duration) by manifest type
- Kube API latency and error rate after upgrade
- Number of resources changed (count) from plan diffs
- IAM failures (403/unauthorized logs) tied to service account creation

Experiment notes (observations so far):

- When adding provider_aws_* outputs we accidentally encouraged direct ARN consumption. Solution: mark provider_aws_* outputs as "provider_metadata" and add a clear README section warning against using provider_ metadata in downstream infra unless guarded.
- Some downstream repos used hardcoded subnet names instead of IDs. Migration requires a small shim module that can read legacy state and produce the expected keys.
- GKE private clusters require special CA handling (client cert vs server CA) — test harness needs at least one GKE native flow with WLID enabled.

Open questions / risks:

- Do we want to expose a single canonical node_role_arn across providers, or enforce provider-specific outputs only? (Recommendation: keep canonical high level, provider-specific for details.)
- How many versions do we support in the compatibility checker? (Recommendation: last 3 major module versions).
- Air‑gapped environments cannot reach our artifact registry for module source tags in some cases. Need a vendored tarball process and a verified checksum workflow.

Next actions / TODOs (owner tags):

- Diego: finalize minimal output contract and update module README (due 2025‑03‑07)
- Aisha: prototype compat‑check script and add to CI (due 2025‑03‑14)
- Samir: provision integration lab topology and run first matrix (due 2025‑03‑10)
- Lena: draft incident rollback runbook and slack templates (due 2025‑03‑12)

Appendix — small snippet of compat-check pseudo output (example):

[compat-check] manifest: customer‑alpha
current-module-outputs: {"vpc_id":"vpc-abc123","subnet_ids":["subnet-1","subnet-2"],"node_role_arn":"arn:aws:iam::..."}
new-module-outputs:     {"vpc_id":"vpc-abc123","private_subnet_ids":["subnet-1"],"node_role_arn":"arn:aws:iam::...","provider_compat_map":"{\"subnet_ids\":\"private_subnet_ids\"}"}
compat-report: downstream reference to subnet_ids -> flagged, suggested migration: replace module.infra.private_subnet_ids or add compatibility shim

Notes to self: keep this doc light and incremental. Expect many small followups. If you are reading this and own a downstream repo that uses top‑level outputs by name, ping Diego and we'll add a short migration helper for your repo.
